title: Saturation simulator for heterogeneous tensor/pipeline parallel meshes
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a deterministic saturation simulator to evaluate tokens/sec and tail-latency (p95/p99) behavior across heterogeneous multi-GPU deployments using tensor parallel (TP) and pipeline parallel (PP) topologies. The simulator will synthesize realistic arrival patterns (steady, bursty, diurnal) and reuse real request traces to reproduce edge cases observed in production. Goals: 1) quantify steady-state throughput and p95 under a range of sequence lengths, KV cache hit rates, and quantized model variants; 2) stress scheduler interactions when TP and PP are mixed across GPUs with different memory/compute profiles; 3) surface regressions automatically via statistical detectors and integrate into CI/nightly regression runs.
approach: Create a workload generator that can replay anonymized production traces and synthetic patterns (Poisson, Pareto bursts, fixed-window microbursts).
Model heterogeneous cluster topologies: combinations of A100/RTX/late-gen GPUs with mismatched VRAM and PCI-E/CCIX crosslinks represented as resource profiles.
Implement instrumentation hooks to capture per-stage latencies for PP stages and per-rank token generation rates for TP groups.
Simulate KV-cache warmup/warmstart behavior and prefix caching to measure cold-vs-warm throughput delta.
Run param sweeps for sequence lengths [64,128,256,1024], batch sizes, kv_cache_hit_rates [0,25,50,75,90], and quantization modes [fp16,int8_quant].
Use statistical regression detectors: rolling baseline + CUSUM and A/B control charts with configurable sensitivity to detect regressions in nightly runs.
Export results to an analysis dashboard (Grafana) and store raw histograms + traces to an S3 bucket for offline analysis.
test_plan: Baseline: single-node homogeneous 8xA100 run to calibrate expected tokens/sec and p95.
Heterogeneous mix: 4xA100 + 2xRTX with PP across GPUs to force uneven stage times; measure stage skew impact.
KV-cache scenarios: cold start, 50% warm, fully warmed; repeat microburst tests to measure p95 spikes.
Network degradation: throttle interconnect bandwidth to emulate noisy neighbor and observe fallback/queueing impact.
Regression injection: introduce a small kernel change that increases stage latency by ~5% and verify detector flags it.
Nightly CI: run fast parity checks (subset of configs) and full sweep weekly.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can reproduce tokens/sec and p95 within 10% of a gold-standard production trace for at least two representative workloads.
Automated detector triggers on synthetic 5% latency regression within configured sensitivity and generates a GitHub issue with links to evidence.
Artifacts (histograms, traces) are uploaded and visible in the Grafana dashboard for every run.
Parameterized sweep scripts and config templates are checked in and documented in the repo.
comments: 2026-02-12: Spike completed to prototype trace replayer and microburst generator. Preliminary results show p95 sensitivity to KV-cache hit rate.
2026-02-23: Design review with runtime team — decided to model heterogeneous GPUs via lightweight capability profiles instead of full device emulation to speed up sweeps.
2026-02-28: Jonah implemented per-stage timing hooks; observed a pathological case where PP stage 2 had 3x variance under burst loads; creating follow-up ENG ticket.
2026-03-03: Added CUSUM-based detector and tuned alpha/beta; false-positive rate acceptable on baseline datasets.
2026-03-09: Integration test failing intermittently due to a race in the synthetic trace loader; assigned to infra on priority.
notes: Trade-offs considered: full device emulation is more accurate but expensive; capability profiles trade some fidelity for 10x faster sweep turnaround.
Potential follow-ups: extend to multi-tenant scenarios and include quantization fallback mixes for mixed-precision deployments.
Risk: noisy neighbor simulation may hide hardware-induced kernel variability; plan to complement simulator with short full-cluster repro runs.
Owner: runtime-performance performance team to maintain the harness after initial development.
